extension.summary: CU LRC Lyrics, fork with OK/OSD, sync, and scraper reliability fixes
extension.description: CU LRC Lyrics (DC Version, Universal) - based on the original CU LRC Lyrics 6.7.1 by Taxigps/ronie (https://gitlab.com/ronie/script.cu.lrclyrics/), plus this fork's own ongoing fixes and improvements: OK-button/OSD focus handling, manual sync and seek with on-screen feedback, more reliable scrapers, and an optional built-in lyrics translation panel that works on any Kodi skin. See this repository's README and the version history below for details.

extension.news: 1.28.1: renamed the addon id from script.cu.lrclyrics.fixed to script.cu.lrclyrics.advanced (per user request - "fixed" implied something was broken/one-off, "advanced" better reflects an actively-developed fork). Kodi treats this as a brand new addon - the old one needs to be uninstalled and this one installed fresh, which also means addon settings (DeepL key, sync offset, etc.) reset to defaults. Also trimmed the 4 translated descriptions way down - they used to itemize every individual fix in prose, now they just say this is based on the original CU LRC Lyrics 6.7.1 plus this fork's own ongoing fixes, and point to the README/news for detail instead of duplicating it. Also updated the RunScript() addon-id references in settings.xml (font install/remove/scraper-test buttons) and script.xderecx.aeonnox5lyricsfix's description to match. 1.28.0: major visual-pass milestone. Root-caused why animations looked broken: font_culrc_current from this addon's own bundled Font.xml never actually loads for a script WindowXMLDialog (confirmed via 5 independent tests logged in kodi.log - defaultRes variations, fontset id collision, a real font-name substitution, a full debug-log walk - not one LoadFontsFromFile call for our path, ever), so all current-line text was silently rendering at a tiny skin-fallback size, making the (correctly working all along) rotate/slide/zoom animations only a couple of pixels and effectively invisible - confirmed live once a real skin font (Estuary's font60) was substituted in for testing. Simplified the current-line display from the previous 5-style/2-digit duplication down to 3 entrance styles (slide from top, slide from left, squash-zoom "landing" from 30%/160% down to 100%/100%) using tween="elastic" easing="out" for a genuine bounce-and-settle instead of a flat linear move. Added lib/fontinstall.py: an opt-in font installer (Settings > Current-line display > "Install decorative fonts into the active skin") that patches 3 real decorative fonts (Exo2-BlackItalic, Ranchers-Regular, Luckiest Guy - all confirmed OFL/Apache licensed and freely redistributable, and confirmed via fontTools to have full Slovak/Czech diacritic glyph coverage) directly into the active skin's own Font.xml, with automatic backup and a matching "Remove decorative fonts" revert action - same technique script.xderecx.aeonnox5lyricsfix already uses for Aeon Nox 5, generalized to any skin installed on writable storage (won't work for a read-only OS-bundled skin, e.g. Estuary on some CoreELEC-style builds - detected and reported, not a crash). Explicitly did NOT bundle Aeon Nox 5's actual "nasalization-rg.ttf" font - its Typodermic Fonts EULA forbids redistribution. Also checked and rejected Fredoka One/PollerOne/Geomancy as decorative options despite free licensing - all three are missing most Slovak/Czech diacritic glyphs, which would have reintroduced the exact bug already fixed earlier in this project. Fixed a pre-existing stale addon-id bug in the scraper-test settings button (was calling RunScript(script.cu.lrclyrics,...) - the pre-fork original addon id, not this fork's script.cu.lrclyrics.fixed). 1.27.4: replaced the 1.27.3 entrance-animation attempt, which turned out to never visibly animate at all (confirmed live - no fade, no motion), with a direct port of Aeon Nox 5's own actual proven mechanism, found by reading script.xderecx.aeonnox5lyricsfix's bundled script-cu-lrclyrics-main.xml.dat. Root cause of the old approach's silence is still unconfirmed (the custom culrc.lineflip window property did verifiably toggle correctly per JSON-RPC polling, so the bug was somewhere in how Kodi's animation engine handled a property-driven group visibility flip) - rather than keep debugging a from-scratch guess, switched to Aeon Nox 5's exact working pattern: 5 entrance styles (slide from top, slide from left, zoom in from 0%, slide from right, zoom in from 400% for a "landing" impact feel) cycling by the last digit of Container(110)/(112).Currentitem - the list's native selected-item position, already live from the existing self.text.selectItem(pos) call, no extra Python property needed at all (removed the now-dead _mark_line_changed()/culrc.lineflip code). Visibility also excludes Container(...).OnNext/OnPrevious, matching Aeon Nox 5, so Kodi's own internal list-scroll transition frame doesn't interfere. Each style has a fixed 4-degree rotation on the outer group (identical value on every style, exactly as Aeon Nox 5 has it) for the scattered/thrown-on-screen look. Per-word coloring is unchanged - still plain per-label textcolor, never inline [COLOR] BBCode, even though the real Aeon Nox 5 file confirms it does use [COLOR] tags for this (the very code path already root-caused to the Slovak/Czech diacritics bug). Also bumped the current-line font to 96 (from 72) per user request and widened/repositioned the word columns to fit. Next step: Aeon Nox 5 also pairs each of these 5 entrance styles with its own distinct font file and size (read directly from the installed skin.aeon.nox.5's Font.xml on the box: nasalization-rg.ttf @76 for the top-slide style, Exo2-BlackItalic.ttf @86 for the left-slide style, nasalization-rg.ttf bold @74 for zoom-in, Ranchers-Regular.ttf @88 for the right-slide style, Ranchers-Regular.ttf @78 for the zoom-landing style) - not yet ported, still using a single NotoSans for all 5 styles. 1.27.3: added entrance animation to the current-line words ("jump onto the screen" per user request, step 2 of the Aeon Nox 5 visual-parity plan). gui.py now tracks the current line index and toggles a new culrc.lineflip window property ('0'/'1') exactly once per distinct line change, via a new _mark_line_changed() helper called from refresh() (the LRC-synced advance loop) and from the initial line select in show_lyrics(). The skin duplicates the current-line word/translation labels into two identical groups, one shown when lineflip=0 and the other when lineflip=1 - since a static visible condition can't retrigger a Visible-trigger animation on every line (it would need to go false-true again, which a value that just stays true never does), alternating between two controls each going hidden-to-visible every other line is the standard Kodi way to get a fresh entrance animation every single line. Each group fades in (200ms) and bounce-slides down from -60px (400ms) on Visible, fades out fast (150ms) on Hidden. Next steps: scattered/varied layout and multiple decorative fonts. 1.27.2: hid the leftover chrome around the current lyric line - artist/title label at top, the small logo/close button top-right, and the scraper-source group bottom (both the context-menu icon bottom-left and the "Zdroj: ..." text bottom-right). None of this was part of the dark box that was already removed in 1.27.1; these were separate always-on controls left over from the original dialog layout. Now the dialog shows only the colored current-line words, matching the plain Aeon Nox 5 style the user is aiming for. 1.27.1: first step of a bigger visual pass toward Aeon Nox 5's look, per user feedback (dark box, no animation, tame layout, small single font) - removed both background-dimming image controls entirely (no box/overlay behind the text at all now, text sits directly over whatever's on screen) and roughly doubled the current-line font size (36 to 72 for the 3 colored words, 30 to 42 for the line below), widening/repositioning their slots to fit. Entrance animations and multiple decorative fonts are separate follow-up steps, not done yet. 1.27.0: the current line now shows per-word coloring inspired by Aeon Nox 5's own style - reviewed ~10 screenshots of Aeon Nox 5's actual variants (some clean 3-color single-line, some wild multi-line rotated/scattered with mixed decorative fonts) and picked the cleanest one as a single fixed layout: the first 3 words in green/yellow/blue, the rest of the line below in white. Uses gui.py's existing get_parts()/part1-4 ListItem properties (already there, untouched from upstream) via separate label controls each with its own plain textcolor - never [COLOR] BBCode inside the label text, since one of the reviewed Aeon Nox 5 screenshots showed a live, concrete example of the known diacritics bug in exactly that rendering path (a gap where a Slovak caron letter should have been). _populate_translation_list() now sets the same part1-4 properties as the original lyrics list so the translation column gets the same per-word coloring. 1.26.2: fixed a real bug found live - no lyric/translation line was ever highlighted at all in the bundled fallback dialog, confirmed via screenshot. Root cause: this dialog deliberately never gives the lyrics/translation list controls real input focus (self.setFocus(self.text) is commented out on purpose, part of the original OK-button-focus-steal fix), and Kodi's list focusedlayout only ever applies to an item with actual control focus, not just the selected-item position from Python - so the bold/colored "current line" style was defined but never once triggered. Added a same-color masking box plus a Container(id).ListItem-bound label directly over each list's own vertical center instead (those infolabels read the selected item regardless of focus), replacing the plain line there with the styled one. 1.26.1: fixed a real crash found live - an empty <default></default> tag on the deepl_api_key string setting made Kodi fail to generate that key at all in a freshly-regenerated addon_data/settings.xml (e.g. after a reinstall), so ADDON.getSettingString('deepl_api_key') threw TypeError: Invalid setting type instead of returning '' - this crashed MAIN.__init__() immediately, taking down lyrics display entirely, not just translation. Fixed the empty default to a proper self-closing <default/>, and wrapped both DeepL-key and Lingva-instance setting reads in gui.py defensively so a single bad/missing setting can never take down the whole service again. 1.26.0: the bundled fallback dialog (resources/skins/Default/) now carries its own font (NotoSans-Regular, SIL OFL, confirmed to have Slovak/Czech diacritics via its cmap table) instead of depending on whatever the active skin defines - consistent typography on any skin, not just skins that happen to define compatible font names. The current/highlighted lyric+translation line is now bigger and bold (font_culrc_current) against dimmed grey surrounding lines (font_culrc_line), for a closer feel to Aeon Nox 5's own colorful styling for this dialog - which turned out, on inspection of its pre-patch backup, to be a native Aeon Nox 5 skin feature that predates any of this repo's work, not something this addon ever provided itself. Deliberately uses only the per-control textcolor tag (never inline [COLOR] BBCode in the label text) for this - the CU LRC diacritics investigation root-caused missing/wrong Slovak/Czech caron letters specifically to Kodi's own [COLOR]-tag text parser on Latin Extended-A characters, so highlighting stays on that safer code path instead of risking reproducing that bug. 1.25.1: added "(Universal)" to the display name so it's clear at a glance in Kodi's Add-ons browser too, not just in the repo README, that this works on any skin. 1.25.0: script.xderecx.aeonnox5lyricsfix is no longer a required dependency - now that 1.24.0 ported the translation panel into this add-on's own bundled dialog, lyrics and translation both work on any Kodi skin without it. Aeon Nox 5's deeper full-screen integration (hidden topbar, rotating fanart, seek overlay, translator credit) remains available as a purely optional companion install for that skin specifically; updated all 4 translated descriptions to stop implying it's needed. This is a deliberate architecture split going forward: this add-on develops as the general, skin-independent lyrics+translation experience, while the Aeon Nox 5 integration is a separate, self-contained branch that is not being extended further. 1.24.1: fixed a real bug found live - a KaraokeTexty merge-window match (2+ consecutive site lines joined with ", " to match one original line) could produce a doubled ",," when the site's own line already ended in a comma (confirmed in a cached translation: "...jsem šilhal,, svět..."). Each line's trailing comma/space is now stripped before rejoining. 1.24.0: found and fixed a real, long-standing crash - GUI.onInit() unconditionally calls self.getControl(112) for the translation list, but the addon's OWN bundled fallback dialog (resources/skins/Default/1080i/script-cu-lrclyrics-main.xml, used on any skin OTHER than the Aeon-Nox-5-patched one) never had a control with that id, so this addon has been crashing immediately on open on every skin except patched Aeon Nox 5 since translation support was added. Ported the translation panel (list id=112, source/coverage textbox, end-of-song human-translator credit label) into that bundled fallback dialog too - widened the window and split it into a left (original lyrics, id=110) / right (translation, id=112) side-by-side layout once a translation is showing, original-only lyrics keeps its old half-width position rather than reflowing to full width (a single control per id is required so onInit()'s one getControl() call can't latch onto a hidden duplicate). This means lyrics + translation now work on ANY Kodi skin, not just Aeon Nox 5 - the seek OSD and standalone credit overlay are still Aeon-Nox-5-only for now. 1.23.3: swapped the per-line machine-filled marker from "† " to "» " per user preference. 1.23.2: hybrid results now mark each individual machine-filled line with a "† " prefix directly in the translation panel, not just as an aggregate percentage in the source strip - confirmed font_translation (NotoSans-Regular) actually has this glyph via its own cmap table before picking it; several tried symbols (gear/star/diamond/lightning, and an actual emoji) are missing from this font and would have rendered as empty boxes. 1.23.1: fixed a real bug found live - a hybrid result's DeepL gap-fill could land in the wrong language even with 1.22.1's cross-fallback fix, because that fix trusted the KaraokeTexty DOMAIN (.sk vs .cz) to know what language its own content is in, and that isn't reliable: confirmed live, karaoketexty.sk served an entirely Czech-language translation column for one song (verified via Czech-only vs Slovak-only diacritic characters - 30 cz-only, 0 sk-only - despite the .sk domain and no cross-fallback suffix on the source name), so the gap-fill correctly followed the addon's Slovak target language while the human-covered lines it was supplementing were actually Czech. human_translation_lang() now detects the ACTUAL fetched content's language via that same diacritic heuristic first, only falling back to the source-name suffix or target_lang when the text is too short/plain to tell (no distinguishing diacritics at all). 1.23.0: fixed a real bug found live - repeating the exact same track (repeat-one, or a short playlist looping back to it) did not restart CU LRC lyrics OR the translation panel at all. Root cause was two separate identity checks that only ever compare artist+title: myPlayerChanged() treated the repeat as "nothing changed" since Song.__eq__ doesn't know about actual playback restarting, so it never even re-fetched lyrics; and even after fixing that, a fresh GUI instance's reset_controls() also only compares an artist|title fingerprint to decide whether to preserve an already-showing translation (needed for the OK/OSD reopen of a still-playing song), which can't tell that apart from a genuine repeat either, and would leave the translation panel WIN properties claiming "shown" while the actual (new) list control was empty. onAVStarted now passes a force flag all the way through myPlayerChanged() and the GUI's kwargs (song_restarted) so a genuine new-playback-start event (Kodi fires onAVStarted again even for an exact repeat) always re-triggers both lyrics and translation, while the OK/OSD same-song reopen path (which doesn't go through onAVStarted) keeps its existing preserve-translation behavior. 1.22.2: fixed a real bug found live testing 1.22.1 - is_fully_human_source() used to treat a cached translation as fully human whenever the CURRENT hybrid marker ("[CR]+") was absent from its source string, but a cache file written under an EARLIER hybrid format (" + " and "(NN% / NN%)", before this session's 2-line "[CR]+" display was introduced) doesn't contain that marker either, so it read as "not hybrid" and got frozen as permanently trusted - confirmed live, a song's translation panel was stuck showing the raw old-format string ("KaraokeTexty + DeepL[CR](92% / 8%)") forever and never re-attempted the new bs4 version at all. is_fully_human_source() now checks the source name against an exact whitelist of the fixed fully-human names instead, which can't be fooled by a hybrid format change since it doesn't try to detect what a hybrid name looks like. 1.22.1: bumped the required beautifulsoup4/soupsieve versions to 4.15.0/2.9.2 (was 4.12.2/2.4.1, matching the box's previously-stuck version) to test whether a scraper-matching discrepancy seen live (a line confirmed identical after normalization both locally and via a fresh page re-fetch, yet still reported as a miss on the box) is actually a bs4-version-specific behavior difference. bs4 4.13+ added a hard runtime dependency on typing_extensions (bs4/_typing.py imports it unconditionally, not just under TYPE_CHECKING), so this also adds a new script.module.typing-extensions (4.16.0) vendored addon. 1.22.0: fixed a real language-mixing bug in the hybrid human+DeepL gap-fill (1.18.0) - the gap-fill DeepL call always translated into self.TRANSLATE_LANG (the requested target language), but a KaraokeTexty cross-fallback human result (source name suffixed "(CS)"/"(SK)") is actually in the OTHER of the two languages, so a Slovak target that fell back to the Czech site could end up with Czech human lines and Slovak DeepL-filled lines mixed in the same translation panel. New lib/humantranslate.py human_translation_lang() derives the gap-fill's target language from the actual human source used instead of always assuming target_lang. 1.21.1: fixed a real bug from 1.21.0 - the hybrid source string format changed to "Name (92%)[CR]+ DeepL (8%)" for the new 2-line display, which broke the "[CR]+"-based hybrid detection this update also had to fix in is_fully_human_source(), and the end-of-song credit's DeepL/percentage stripping (previously done by splitting the display string on " + ", which no longer appears literally in the new format). The credit name is now tracked in its own culrc.translation.credit_source property instead of being parsed back out of the display string at all. 1.21.0: the translation-panel source strip (script-cu-lrclyrics-main.xml.dat, now a 2-line textbox instead of a single-line label) shows a hybrid "KaraokeTexty + DeepL" result as two lines - the source names, then the human/machine coverage percentage on its own line - instead of a single truncated line. 1.20.1: reworked the fuzzy last-resort tier from a character-level similarity percentage to a word-level diff count (still via difflib.SequenceMatcher, just fed word lists instead of raw strings) - a fixed percentage threshold penalizes short lines unfairly (a single wrong word in a 4-word line can drop the character-ratio to 70-80%, well under any reasonable threshold, while the same single-word difference barely dents a long line's ratio), whereas "at most one differing word" means the same thing regardless of line length, confirmed with both long and short synthetic test lines. Requires at least 3 words on both sides so a 1-2 word line can't trivially match almost anything. 1.20.0: added a fourth, absolute-last-resort matching tier using Python's standard difflib.SequenceMatcher for a line that's genuinely a near-miss - a wording variant between the two sources rather than a formatting difference. Every match now logs which of the four tiers found it. 1.19.1: a hybrid "KaraokeTexty + DeepL" result (see 1.18.0's gap-filling) is no longer cached forever - only a FULLY human match is, since a hybrid one might improve to a better ratio (or full human coverage) later, whether from a matching-logic improvement or the site's own content changing, and re-checking it on the next view is cheap. The end-of-song credit still shows for a cached hybrid result exactly as before, this only changes whether it's re-attempted. 1.19.0: added a third, last-resort content-matching tier for KaraokeTexty alignment - after exact single-line and merge-window matching both fail for a line, tries again with internal whitespace removed too (not just punctuation), catching a word split differently across a line-break or hyphenation quirk between the two sources. This tier is strictly more permissive than the other two (dropping word boundaries can in principle equate two genuinely different phrases), so it only ever runs after they've both already failed for that line, and every match now logs which of the three tiers found it. 1.18.3: the end-of-song translation credit no longer mentions DeepL for a hybrid "KaraokeTexty + DeepL" result - DeepL only filled in a few lines the human source didn't cover, it didn't do the actual translation, so the thank-you message now credits just the human site/translator. 1.18.2: apostrophes are now deleted entirely rather than treated as a word boundary when normalizing lines for comparison - two independently-transcribed sources commonly differ on whether a contraction keeps its apostrophe at all (e.g. "don't" vs "dont"), and unlike other punctuation it sits inside a word, so turning it into a space like the rest would wrongly split one word into two instead of unifying the spellings. 1.18.1: fixed a real bug in the line-merge logic - a "line" that's purely punctuation (e.g. a standalone ellipsis used as its own <br>-separated line to mark a pause/trail-off, where the original combines it into the surrounding line with a comma instead) normalizes to nothing and has no real content to align on, but keeping it as its own pairs entry broke the merge-window check, which stopped at the first empty entry instead of skipping past it - confirmed live on a real song. These punctuation-only "lines" are now dropped entirely when parsing each column, so real content lines stay adjacent and merge correctly across where they used to sit. 1.18.0: KaraokeTexty content alignment no longer requires 100% coverage to be used at all - a partial human match now keeps every line it did find (tagged e.g. "KaraokeTexty + DeepL") and machine-translates only the specific remaining gaps (e.g. a chorus the fan site never wrote out in the original language, so there was nothing to match against at all), instead of discarding the whole human result and falling back to pure machine translation for the entire song. 1.17.1: widened the line-merge window from 2-3 to 2-5 consecutive site lines when checking whether they combine to match one original line. 1.17.0: KaraokeTexty content alignment now also matches when a single original (timed) line corresponds to several consecutive lines on the fan site - e.g. our LRC has one line combining two short phrases with a comma, while the site writes each phrase as its own <br>-separated line (confirmed live on a real song, this was a real source of low match rates, not missing content). Exact single-line matches are still tried and applied first; only lines with no direct match fall through to checking 2-3-line merge windows. 1.16.0: once the last timed lyric line has passed, if a human translation source was used (LyricsTranslate/KaraokeTexty, never DeepL/Google/Lingva), shows a "translation by X, support them at Y" credit for ~25s - includes the individual credited translator's name when KaraokeTexty shows one. Fixed a real bug found while adding this: KaraokeTexty's translator-credit link is nested inside the same span as the last translated line with no <br> separating it, so it was silently glued onto the end of that line's text before this fix, corrupting its content-match against the original. Requires script.xderecx.aeonnox5lyricsfix 1.6.0+ for the new skin overlay. 1.15.2: addon description (all 4 translated languages) now mentions the human-translation-first behavior and the Czech<->Slovak cross-fallback, was undocumented before. 1.15.1: normalized punctuation/quote-style before comparing lines for KaraokeTexty content alignment (curly vs straight apostrophes, commas/periods, double spacing) - a single differing character was failing an otherwise-identical line's match, confirmed live (one song matched only 9/32 lines before this fix). 1.15.0: KaraokeTexty.sk/.cz human translations are now aligned by CONTENT instead of only by total line count - the scraper now keeps both the original-language and translated columns (not just the translation) and matches each of the addon's own original lyric lines against KaraokeTexty's original-language lines to find its translation, reusing the same translation for a repeated line (e.g. a chorus sung multiple times) even when the fan site only wrote it out once or twice. Falls back to machine translation only if any original line has no match at all (100% coverage required, no partial results). LyricsTranslate still uses the simpler exact-count check for now, since its original-language text isn't in the same page load. 1.14.4: vendored this addon's module dependencies (beautifulsoup4, chardet, mutagen, requests, and requests'/beautifulsoup4's own sub-dependencies soupsieve/urllib3/certifi/idna) as real addon packages in this repository instead of relying only on Kodi's official repo for them, and bumped the declared minimum versions to match what's actually shipped/tested (was pinned to matrix-era minimums from the original fork, e.g. beautifulsoup4 4.8.2 vs the 4.12.2 actually in use). 1.14.3: fixed a real bug in the KaraokeTexty.sk/.cz scraper - the old bs4 4.8.2 bundled with this Kodi build silently drops some lines when using col.find_all('br') + br.replace_with('\n') on this site's markup (confirmed: modern bs4 gets the full line count from the identical page, old bs4 loses some - reproduced the exact discrepancy directly against bs4==4.8.2). Replaced with a plain regex split on the column's raw inner HTML, which doesn't depend on that bs4 API and gets the correct count on both old and new bs4. 1.14.2: fixed a real bug in the human-translation line-count check for timed lyrics - self.pOverlay (and therefore the original-lines array) includes blank entries for bare timing markers with no lyric text, which a scraped human translation never has, so the comparison was checking against the wrong (too-high) count and would have misaligned every line after the first blank marker had it ever matched. Now compares against the non-empty line count and splices matching human lines back into their original non-empty positions, leaving blank timing-marker slots blank. 1.14.1: fixed a real bug in 1.14.0 - a pre-existing machine-translation cache file (e.g. from before this version) was trusted forever and never re-attempted, so a song already translated once via DeepL/Google/Lingva would never actually try the new human sources at all. Now only a cached HUMAN translation is trusted; any cached DeepL/Google/Lingva result is always re-attempted (human sources first) on the next view. 1.14.0: new lib/humantranslate.py adds human (non-machine) translation sources tried before DeepL/Google/Lingva - LyricsTranslate.com (all 5 addon languages, discovered via a DuckDuckGo site: search since LT's own search is behind an unsolvable Cloudflare challenge from a scripted request) and KaraokeTexty.sk/.cz (Slovak/Czech only, with a Slovak-Czech cross-fallback when only the other of the two exists, since the two languages are close enough to be a better stand-in than machine translation). For timed lyrics, a human translation is only used if its line count matches the original exactly (a human translator doesn't preserve line boundaries the way translating the exact same array does) - otherwise falls through to machine translation as before. For untimed lyrics any line count is fine. A cached human translation is never re-fetched or downgraded. 1.13.2: updated the one-time first-timed-lyrics tip notification (string #32012), which only ever mentioned Up/Down sync and was now stale since 1.10.0 added Left/Right seek - now mentions both. 1.13.1: widened the lyrics sync-offset slider range (context menu "Sync", or up/down on timed lyrics) from ±20s to ±30s. 1.13.0: skip translating lyrics into English when they're already in English (target language = English only) - a cheap stopword-frequency heuristic (lib/translate.py looks_like_english(), not a real language detector) avoids burning DeepL/Google/Lingva quota on a no-op translation, for both manual "Show translation" and "sticky" auto-translate on a new track. Only applied for an English target, since the same short-circuit for the other 4 languages would need a reliable stopword list per language to do safely without risking skipping a translation that was actually needed. 1.12.0: new unified "Interface & translation language" setting (English default, plus Español/Deutsch/Slovenčina/Čeština) - one choice now drives both this add-on's own menus/notifications/dialogs (via a new lib/localization.py that reads the matching resources/language/resource.language.xx_yy/strings.po directly, independent of Kodi's own system language) and the default lyrics translation target language, replacing the old separate free-text translate_lang setting (previously constrained to sk/cs only). Added full cs_CZ, es_ES and de_DE translations (sk_SK and en_GB already existed) plus matching addon.xml description/summary entries for Kodi's Add-ons browser (that part still follows Kodi's system language, a Kodi limitation - only this add-on's own runtime strings follow the new setting). 1.11.2: fixed a real bug - the highlighted lyric line did not reliably follow a seek (either left/right or clicking a line to jump to it). refresh() only ever reschedules its own timer for the NEXT line boundary, computed from the position BEFORE the seek, so the display kept following the pre-seek timeline until that stale timer happened to fire on its own, which could take several seconds and looked like lyrics not reacting to seeking at all. Both seek paths now force an immediate stop_refresh()+refresh() right after seekTime() instead of waiting on the stale timer. 1.11.1: bumped script.xderecx.aeonnox5lyricsfix requirement to 1.5.0 for the repositioned/widened seek overlay (no library code change). 1.11.0: left/right seek now shows a transient progress-bar overlay (position on the full track timeline, elapsed/total time, and the +/-10s/30s/1:00 amount just seeked) matching Kodi's own video seek OSD style, auto-hiding after ~1.5s of no further presses - since this dialog swallows the native seek OSD entirely, seeking previously gave no visual feedback at all about where it landed. Requires script.xderecx.aeonnox5lyricsfix 1.3.0+ for the new skin controls. 1.10.0: large batch of translation and sync fixes. Translation: added a direct Google Translate fallback tier (DeepL to Google to Lingva) since it's the same engine Lingva proxies but doesn't depend on a specific public instance's uptime; translation is now "sticky" for the rest of the session once turned on - a new song reuses its cache or fetches a fresh one automatically, same as pressing "Show translation" manually; a cached Google/Lingva result gets upgraded to DeepL automatically once a DeepL key is available again; the translation panel now fills in progressively as each line arrives instead of staying blank for 20-30s on the Google/Lingva per-line fallback (and this now also correctly finishes for DeepL's single batch call, which was a real bug - the panel used to get stuck showing the original untranslated text until a full reopen); context menu label now toggles between "Show translation" and "Hide translation" instead of always reading the same regardless of state; missing Slovak strings.po entries for the last few versions' new strings (was silently falling back to English) are filled in. Sync offset: fixed a real bug where the offset appeared to reset after the OK/OSD reopen or a next-track change - self.syncadjust is now the single source of truth (read directly from the lyrics file's own [offset:N] tag every time, instead of being split between that tag and a separately-tracked live delta that only one of two code paths knew about); the sync slider now runs in its own dedicated skin window (see script.xderecx.aeonnox5lyricsfix 1.2.0) instead of the shared DialogSlider.xml also used for volume/seek/brightness elsewhere in Kodi. Other: a fast local .lrc lookup could lose a race against the previous song's GUI thread still cleaning up, silently skipping showing lyrics (and therefore translation) entirely until a manual OK/OSD reopen forced a retry - now waits up to ~2s for that cleanup instead of giving up immediately; left/right on the remote now seeks the track (this dialog was swallowing all input, including the seek that normally works with no dialog open at all), with the same rapid-repeat acceleration as Kodi's video seek OSD (10s / 30s / 60s). 1.9.0: translation now falls back to a free Lingva Translate instance (no key needed, auto-detects source language) when no DeepL key is set, or when DeepL fails/runs out of its one-time character credit - previously it just showed an error in that case. The Lingva instance used is configurable in settings in case the default (lingva.ml) goes down. 1.8.0: added an optional, off-by-default lyrics translation feature (context menu "Show translation") using the DeepL API - requires an API key set in this addon's settings. On-demand only (never fetched automatically per song, to avoid burning API quota on tracks you don't care about), and the result is cached as a plain text file alongside the addon's own saved lyrics so it's only translated once per song. 1.7.0: now declares script.xderecx.aeonnox5lyricsfix as a real add-on dependency, so Kodi installs it automatically alongside this one instead of it being an easy-to-miss separate manual step - it still needs to be run once from Program add-ons to actually patch the skin (can't auto-patch a third-party skin without the user's OK). Also now auto-disables the original script.cu.lrclyrics on every Kodi startup if it's found installed and enabled, since the two can't both run as the lyrics service - previously this conflict had to be resolved manually. 1.6.0: up/down during timed lyrics now opens the same on-screen slider dialog used by the context menu's "Sync" option, instead of silently nudging a hidden offset and popping a "Sync offset: +0.5s" notification that didn't say which direction was which. The slider dialog has a static "LATER <---- SYNC OFFSET ----> EARLIER" legend plus a live readout ("Lyrics play Xs earlier/later"/"In sync"), auto-closes after 4s of no input, and the slider step matches the old 0.5s nudge. 1.5.2: clear the previous song's lyrics from the screen immediately on song change, instead of leaving the old lyrics visible for the few seconds get_lyrics() can take to run scraper lookups for the new song. 1.5.1: fixed the same native Kodi crash as 1.5.0 recurring, because 1.5.0 only excluded the ".offset(N)" + "MusicPlayer.Duration" combination while the next-song lyrics prefetch (Song.next(), added for the duration-aware filtering in 1.4.0) still queried Title/Artist/Lyrics/Property with ".offset(1)" - it turns out any MusicPlayer/Player info label combined with ".offset(N)" is unsafe on this Kodi build, not just Duration. Song.next() is now disabled entirely (returns None) instead of trying to fix each individual label one crash at a time - prefetching next-song lyrics was a minor head-start optimization, not essential, since lyrics still get fetched reactively the moment the next track actually starts. 1.5.0: fixed a Kodi crash (native SIGSEGV inside CGUIInfoManager::GetMultiInfoLabel, called via xbmc.getInfoLabel from Python) observed shortly after Song.by_offset() queried "MusicPlayer.offset(N).Duration" for the prefetched next-song lookup added in 1.4.0's duration-aware filtering. That exact info label combination (Duration + a non-zero offset) is far less established than plain "MusicPlayer.Duration", so duration is now only fetched for the current song (offset 0) rather than trying to root-cause a native crash inside Kodi itself. 1.4.0: restored manual lyrics sync correction - the old scrolltosync() feature relied on the lyrics list having native focus (self.controlId == 110) to read a manually-navigated line's timestamp, which was dead code ever since focus was disabled in 1.0.0 for the OK-button/OSD fix, so up/down did nothing for out-of-sync (but correct-edit) timed lyrics. Up/down during timed lyrics now directly nudges a saved offset (with an on-screen readout) instead of depending on focus. Also added duration-aware filtering to the lrclib and musixmatchlrc scrapers so a title/artist match to a different edit (radio edit, remix, extended version) with a different length is rejected instead of producing badly out-of-sync lyrics. 1.3.0: fixed plain (untimed) txt lyrics getting stuck showing only the first line forever - a regression from the 1.0.0 OK-button/OSD fix, which disabled focus on the lyrics list so onFocus() (and the up/down scroll handling that depended on it) never fired. Timed LRC lyrics were unaffected since those auto-scroll via a timer regardless of focus. Up/down now moves the txt lyrics selection directly. 1.2.0: fixed a false-positive match in the Music163 scraper - it sometimes only has songwriter/composer credit lines in its lyric DB (e.g. "作词 : ..." / "作曲 : ...") with no actual lyrics, but returned them as if they were valid, blocking the real Genius/musixmatch result from being tried. Now checks the returned lyric actually has content beyond credit lines. 1.1.0: fixed a bug where the lrclib.net scraper could crash with an uncaught TypeError when the API returned an unexpected (non-list) response, which silently aborted the entire remaining lyrics search cascade (musixmatch, genius, supermusic, etc. never got tried). The lrclib scraper is now defensive against bad responses, and both scraper loops in gui.py now catch exceptions per-provider so one broken source can no longer block the rest. 1.0.0: fork of upstream 6.7.1. Fixed OK button being swallowed by lyrics dialog focus; OK now shows OSD and lyrics auto-resume when OSD closes.
